claims.text: For adults with low levels of frailty (frailty index score ≤ 0.1), sedentary time is not predictive of mortality regardless of physical activity level.
Among vulnerable adults (0.1 < frailty index score ≤ 0.2) who are physically inactive, sedentary time is associated with higher mortality.
Among frail adults (frailty index score > 0.2) who are physically inactive, sedentary time is associated with higher mortality.
The effect of sedentary behaviors on mortality varies by the degree of frailty.

evidence.description: Adjusted HR of 0.90 (95% CI 0.70-1.15) for sedentary time in adults with frailty index score ≤ 0.1.
HR of 1.16 (95% CI 1.02-1.33) for sedentary time among physically inactive individuals in the 0.1 < frailty index score ≤ 0.2 group.
HR of 1.27 (95% CI 1.11-1.46) for frailty index score 0.2-0.3 and HR 1.34 (95% CI 1.19-1.50) for frailty index score > 0.3 among physically inactive adults.
Cox proportional hazard models demonstrated varying hazard ratios of mortality across frailty score strata, with the highest frailty level showing the greatest adverse impact.

methodologies.name: Prospective cohort analysis with Cox proportional hazard models
methodologies.description: Evaluated the interaction between accelerometer-measured sedentary time, a 46-item frailty index, physical activity level, and all-cause mortality.
datasets: 2003/04 and 2005/06 cohorts of the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
conditions: 3141 community-dwelling adults aged 50 years or older
Sedentary time measured via uniaxial accelerometers
Frailty categorized via a 46-item frailty index
